messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content:
In lions, one of the most well‑documented dominant traits is the **presence of a mane in adult male lions**. The mane is a secondary sexual characteristic that is largely governed by a dominant allele (often referred to as the “mane” allele). Males that inherit this allele will develop a mane, while females and males lacking the allele do not.

Other dominant traits in lions include:

| Trait | Gene/Allele | Dominance |
|-------|-------------|-----------|
| Tawny coat color | *MC1R* (melanocortin 1 receptor) allele | Dominant |
| Large body size (within normal range) | *IGF1* (insulin‑like growth factor 1) allele | Dominant |

These dominant alleles are expressed in the phenotype when present, even if only one copy is inherited from either parent.
